page0.text: But still...right now, I have to stop Illya!

page1.text:
"No, come back, Illya!"
I run out from the cover of the trees.
Illya's running at Berserker.
I catch up to her and pull her back.
...In my ears gone numb from stress, the fierce howling of the wind and the mad warrior's roars
buffet me so violently I can't even see.

page2.text:
The wind pushes me to the ground, Illya still in my arms.
My vision's gone white, and I can't even stand.
...No.
I can't even remember to stand.

page3.text:
...
...My body is hot.
Something sleeping deep within Shirou Emiya cries out.
I don't know what or why, but I sense this heat resonating with the Noble Phantasm that was just unleashed.

page5.text:
It's getting as hard to breathe as it is to see.
I can't do anything.
As long as that sword is burned into my eyes, none of my human functions will be restored.

page7.text:
It's like I'm under a spell.
My heart was stolen by something I only caught sight of for a brief instant.

page8.text:
...Even among the numerous Noble Phantasms, it's an illusion of a different magnitude.
Few Noble Phantasms can rival its elegant design and fine worksmanship.
But its beauty is hardly skin deep.
No, the word "beautiful" would be an insult to this sword.

page9.text:
The sword isn't beautiful, but earnest and precious.
It's a legend imbued with the hopes and dreams of the people.
Neither a relic of myth nor a work of mankind, it is a crystallization crafted from our feelings alone—a sword of pure fantasy, sitting at the apex.

page10.text:
My eyesight returns.
Black, crimson flame as dark as midnight illuminates the sky.
Was the pillar of light that cleaved the forest darkness itself?
The flames burn silently, but the air is cold.
Maybe it doesn't burn oxygen, but freezes it, instead.
The darkly lit forest grows colder.

page11.text:
...
A swordsman stands against the backdrop of black flames.
I scowl at the sword pointed at me, one of my arms still around Illya.

page12.text:
I can't feel any bloodlust or hostility from the swordsman.
I'm afraid of being killed, but at the same time, I clench my jaw in frustration.

page13.text:
—It's not her.
This is someone else.
It's not just her lack of malice.
She...
She doesn't have any of the nobility she used to.

page14.text:
Her helm cracks.
It must have been thanks to Berserker's last attack.
When I see her bare face, I know without a doubt that it's her, no matter how much she's changed.

page15.text:
"Sa...ber..."
...
She doesn't reply.
Her eyes are now gold and unreadable. They just stare down at me, her fallen foe.

page16.text:
"...Shirou."
Illya's voice is trembling.
Behind Saber, something that looks like the eviscerated corpse of Berserker sinks into the dark Shadow.
Illya just watched her Servant die in battle.
Of course a young girl like her would be scared.

page17.text:
"...Saber."
I shake off the excess emotions.
I hold on tight to Illya, and tense my right arm.

page18.text:
This isn't the time to be shocked.
I'm going to save Illya.
I'll save her and go home.
I can't freeze in my tracks here and wait for death...!

page19.text:
"...!"
Saber swings her sword.
Just as she's about to cut me down while I'm trying to stand up, she instantly changes direction and deflects three arrows.

page20.text:
"Archer...!?"
"Don't stop! Take Illya and get out of there!"
Swords clash.
Archer immediately follows his sniping up with a bladed assault.

page21.text:
"Ngh...!"
"..."
But it doesn't give me any peace of mind.
Saber easily blocks his blindingly fast dual swords.

page22.text:
"Gurgh...!"
Something's wrong with Archer.
I look and see that his feet are tangled in the Shadow, too.

page23.text:
"What a disgrace, Archer.
A pure Heroic Spirit could never resist that thing's cursed realm. Right now, you are little different from the wraiths roaming these woods."

page24.text:
...That ruthless voice definitely belongs to Saber.
She nonchalantly steps on the Shadow, and...
"Guh...!"
Effortlessly sends Archer flying into the woods behind him.

page25.text:
"Wha..."
Even if the Shadow was slowing him down, she cut right through both of his swords' guard without even trying.

page26.text:
...
...Then, she does it again.
Saber faces me silently.
Those eyes...
They declare that she'll kill me unless I hand Illya over.

page27.text:
"...Shirou."
Illya lets go of my arm.
The gesture seems to say that it's okay to hand her over. It flips a switch inside me.

page28.text:
"Get back. Tohsaka's waiting for us in the woods. We'll figure this out if we can get back there."
I push Illya back and take hold of my wooden sword with my now free left hand.

page29.text:
...I take a seigan stance.
If Saber comes for us, I'll use all the strength and magical energy I have to strike back.
...
That's all I can do now.
I have nothing to say to Saber.
I can't apologize, nor can I ask her to come back to me.
She isn't speaking to me, so that isn't something I should say to her.
Saber is my enemy now.
The only way I can respond is to fight back as hard as I can.
"Ngh..."
...I tighten my aim.
I won't try for a mutual kill. Saber personally taught me that it isn't an effective tactic.
An attack that risks your own life only works when you're evenly matched with your opponent.
I can't hope to achieve that against Saber.
So, I'm only going to try one attack.
Now that her helmet is broken, I should be able to do some damage if I go for the head.
It will take everything I have.
I'll defeat my enemy and survive.
Unless I imagine myself fully committing to this, I don't have a chance against her...!
...
Here she comes...!
Dodge, dodge, dodge, dodge...!
Who cares if it looks bad, who cares if I have to crawl in the mud, if I can't dodge the first attack, then forget protecting Illya...!

page31.text:
—I'm dead.
I've sparred rashly with Saber enough times to know that she won this bout.
Her downstroke streaks down like a diving falcon, from my upper left.
It's a slash precise enough to cut a grain of rice, coming for Shirou Emiya's head.

page32.text:
But...
My head stays attached.
Saber's sword stops just shy of my neck.

page33.text:
...
...What happened?
Then, she wordlessly lowers her sword, and turns away.

page34.text:
"...!"
Don't tell me she stopped her sword because of that.
The black swamp spreading across the ground.
That Shadow is trying to crawl out of it.

page35.text:
...There's no doubt.
It's that unknown being, that clump of curses
that I saw before in the park...

page36.text:
"My role is finished here. I leave the rest to you."
"My gratitude. It is an easy task. With this, I can restore my honor for losing to that Majnun."
Saber walks deeper into the black swamp.

page37.text:
And then...
She sinks into the Shadow with a bubbling noise, just like Berserker.

page38.text:
...
I watch until she's gone.
—I have no way of knowing why she's still in this world, or why she's on their side now.
If she's my enemy, then I have to fight her.
That's what war is.

page39.text:
...
But, still...
I can't help but think that if I had been stronger that night, she might never have been warped into that dark version of herself.

page40.text:
"Emiya...!"
"..."
Tohsaka's voice pulls me back to reality.
Right now, we're facing the creeping black Shadow and the Assassin with the skull mask locked into a smile.
